strengths: The recruiter starts from the currently trusted person and explicitly chooses the page to fold in, so the dominant decision is 'which identity stays stable' rather than a symmetric database merge.
The review exposes relationship names, source counts, confirmed-fact counts, label differences, masked identity clues, and blockers before changing ownership.
The Agent opens the real structured review from Chat and reports a concrete completed or staged operation instead of presenting a conversational promise.
Two relationship contexts remain separate working contexts after merge; the product does not flatten candidate, client, referral, or search histories into one generic profile.
The people picker now performs account-scoped server search instead of being limited to the twenty most recent directory entries.

An applied merge can be reopened after reload from durable Agent history; the fresh review shows current ownership and the original reason, and a successful split follows the restored relationship to its real person page.

findings.observation: Name and context search is account scoped and server backed, but the workflow does not yet rank likely duplicates from confirmed identifiers or recent intake.
findings.user_impact: The flow can repair a known duplicate but still relies on the recruiter to notice and locate it.
findings.recommendation: Offer evidence-backed duplicate suggestions at intake or on the person page using exact confirmed handles and recruiter-visible match reasons; never auto-merge from a name.
findings.verification: In a large synthetic directory, exact confirmed-handle candidates appear first with masked evidence, same-name candidates remain suggestions, and no suggestion changes identity without review.

findings.observation: The complete local loop reduces reconciliation steps in a synthetic case, but no working recruiter comparison is attached.
findings.user_impact: Product coherence is proven; workflow superiority and willingness to reuse are not.
findings.recommendation: Run timed duplicate-repair and pre-call reconstruction comparisons with independent recruiters using consented data.
findings.verification: Measure completion time, incorrect merge rate, correction burden, lost-context rate, and willingness to reuse against the recruiter's current notes or ATS fallback.

strengths: The mutation requires current source and target versions, an exact preview digest, a recruiter reason, and an explicit merge decision.
A late source invalidates the preview; an unresolved identity case or unresolved external effect blocks the operation.
Confirmed handles stay masked in review, raw values are not promoted, and no identifier is discarded by merge.
The source person is marked merged rather than deleted, old URLs resolve to the retained person, and reversal restores recorded ownership arrays.
Reversal fails closed if new evidence, confirmed state, or research now depends on a moved relationship context.
Durable history reopens a read-only eligibility review that recomputes current identity, ownership, and dependencies; blocked execution is enforced by the backend as well as the Web.
All affected Wikis are invalidated and recompiled; audit events distinguish merge, reversal, and derived compilation.
The Web mutation routes require authentication, same-origin mutation, JSON content type, bounded identifiers, and idempotency keys.
The operation performs no message, calendar, contact, ATS, CRM, or other external write.
The narrow responsive surface keeps the person identity, retained direction, and source inventory readable without converting the review into a dense CRM table.
Fold-in and retain cards stack vertically with a directional arrow, and the decision button expands to a 44-pixel full-width target.
Text labels accompany color for selected, retained, blocked, applied, and reversed states.
The receipt and undo review remain in the same evidence order as the desktop surface.

findings.observation: Authenticated desktop and responsive-narrow dark surfaces were inspected, but the browser viewport override did not produce a verified 390-pixel viewport in this run.
findings.user_impact: Smallest-iPhone wrapping, keyboard obstruction, VoiceOver order, Dynamic Type, safe-area behavior, and interruption recovery remain unproven.
findings.recommendation: Run this exact merge, stale-preview, blocked, and reversal flow in iOS Simulator at the smallest supported size with VoiceOver and large text.
findings.verification: No horizontal overflow, clipped retained identity, hidden confirmation, nested scroll trap, duplicate submission, or lost receipt occurs across background and resume.

agreements: The retained person plus separate relationship contexts is the correct canonical model.
Chat should open and explain structured identity work, not execute an opaque model-selected merge.
The local slice is materially complete only because preview, optimistic concurrency, compilation, redirect, audit, and reversal were all proven together.
Production and commercial claims still require exact mobile accessibility proof and working-recruiter field comparison.
adjudication.next_priority: Run the exact merge and recovery flow on iOS Simulator, then compare it with current duplicate-repair work using independent recruiters.
